source: NCERT Class VII, Our Pasts II, History Ch. 6.

sections.heading: 1. Types of Towns
points: Medieval towns were of several kinds — often a town was **more than one type at once**:

sub: **Temple towns** — grew around big temples (e.g. **Thanjavur, Madurai, Kanchipuram, Tirupati**); temples were patrons of crafts and trade.
**Commercial towns** and **port towns** — hubs of trade.

points: Towns had **markets, temples/mosques, artisans' quarters** and were usually **densely populated**.

sections.heading: 2. Temple Towns and Pilgrimage
points: Rulers **endowed temples** with land and money; temples employed many people and became centres of **craft, trade and banking**.
**Pilgrims** made donations, boosting the town's economy.
**Thanjavur** (Rajarajeshvara temple) is a classic temple town; **bronze-casting** and other crafts flourished there.

sections.heading: 3. Crafts and Craftspersons
points: Specialised crafts: **weaving, dyeing, metalwork, bronze images, jewellery**.
**Bidri** work — inlay of silver/gold on a **zinc–copper alloy**, from **Bidar** (Deccan).
The **Saliyar / Kaikkolar** weavers and the **Panchalas / Vishwakarma** community (goldsmiths, bronzesmiths, blacksmiths, carpenters, masons) were important artisan groups.
Crafts were often **hereditary** and organised in **communities**.

sections.heading: 4. Trade and Traders
points: India traded via **Gujarat (Cambay/Surat), the Malabar coast, and the Coromandel coast**.
**Surat** = the **'gateway to the West'** and to **Mecca** (Hajj pilgrimage & trade).
**Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam)** and **Hampi (Vijayanagara)** were bustling trade/urban centres.
**Guilds** of traders (e.g. the **Manigramam** and **Nanadesi** in the south) financed trade over long distances.
**European trading companies** (Portuguese, Dutch, English) set up factories at ports — reshaping trade.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Town types: temple, administrative, commercial, port (often overlapping).
Temple towns: Thanjavur, Madurai, Kanchipuram, Tirupati.
Bidri work = silver/gold inlay on zinc-copper alloy (Bidar).
Surat = gateway to the West and to Mecca; Masulipatnam & Hampi = major centres.
Southern merchant guilds: Manigramam, Nanadesi.
European companies set up port 'factories' (Portuguese/Dutch/English).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Bidri** craft is named after **Bidar** and uses a **zinc-copper alloy** with silver/gold inlay.
**Surat** was the gateway for the **Hajj/Mecca** trade and the western sea route.
A 'factory' at a port then meant a **warehouse/trading station**, not a manufacturing plant.
Temple towns grew around **temples as economic hubs**, not only as places of worship.
